baseline.label: Baseline
baseline.description: Quick sanity check: short generation, JSON output, factual recall, instruction following, list format. Fast first-pass to weed out broken models.

tool_calling.label: Tool Calling
tool_calling.description: Does the model pick the right tool, with valid arguments, in the right order? 6 mocked tools, 8 tasks covering single calls, sequences, error recovery and ambiguity.

rag.label: RAG
rag.description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over a fictional corpus (Helion Robotics). 50 Q&A in 3 tiers: factual single-doc, multi-doc synthesis, and out-of-corpus honesty checks.

planning.label: Planning
planning.description: LangGraph planning + execution. Each task runs in mode 4a (model plans for itself) and 4b (given a canonical plan) so we can isolate planning ability from execution.

personal_agent.label: Personal Agent
personal_agent.description: 20-turn conversation with mid-thread tool calls and recall probes. Measures context memory, tool fidelity over long history, and latency drift as context grows.

multi_agent.label: Multi-agent
multi_agent.description: Multi-role research workflow Researcher → Critic → Writer via LangGraph. Tests collaboration between roles and the quality of the final synthesised report.

tests.tasksDescription: Open a suite to see its individual tasks and (for RAG) the corpus + the prompts used to generate it.

home.heroTagline: Benchmark your local AI models like an Olympic decathlon.
home.heroSubtitle: OLLAMPICS runs your Ollama models through agentic tasks — tool calling, RAG, multi-turn conversation, planning, multi-agent workflows — and gives you a clean comparison of how each model performs.
home.whatIs1: A benchmark harness for local LLMs. Each model competes in the same tasks; results are stored in SQLite and visualised in this app. Designed for people who run Ollama locally and want hard data on which model fits which job.
home.whatIs2: Every run captures throughput, time-to-first-token, VRAM, tokens, retries and a success/fail verdict per task — so you can compare quantizations, models, or runtime configs apples to apples.
home.howStep1: Browse the Ollama library and pull the models you want to test. Anything Ollama can run, OLLAMPICS can benchmark.
home.howStep2: Open the Tests page to see the six suites available — Baseline (sanity check), Tool Calling, RAG, Planning, Personal Agent, Multi-agent. Each card tells you what it measures.
home.howStep3: From Launcher, tick the models and suites you want, set num_ctx and KV cache, then Launch. You'll see live progress, and afterwards the Leaderboard ranks the models.

tps.name: tps (tokens/s)
tps.desc: Decode throughput — tokens generated per second during the answer phase. Higher = faster output.

ttft.name: ttft (ms)
ttft.desc: Time to first token. The model's reaction time. Lower = more responsive.

tokensIn.name: tok_in
tokensIn.desc: Prompt tokens the model processed for this task.

vram.name: vram
vram.desc: Peak VRAM (MB) the model occupied while running. Reported by ollama ps.

watts.name: watts
watts.desc: Average GPU power draw (opt-in via powermetrics, requires sudo on macOS).

successRate.name: success_rate
successRate.desc: Fraction of tasks the model passed. A task passes when its verifier (regex / schema / LLM judge) returns OK.

tries.name: tries
tries.desc: Average attempts the model needed to pass (some tasks allow retries on failure).

home.addTests1: Tests are plain YAML files in tasks/<suite>/. Drop a new YAML in (or copy an existing one) with prompt, verifier and max_tries — it gets discovered automatically on the next run.
home.addTests2: For RAG specifically, the corpus is generated by an agent (LangGraph + DeepSeek). Go to Tests → RAG, click Generate corpus, edit the prompts on disk to tune what the agent produces.
home.addModels1: All models come from your local Ollama install. Browse the catalog, pull what you want, then re-open OLLAMPICS — discovered models show up automatically on the Launcher.
